To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of hyperoxia depend on the tumor cell type and that the effects of oxygen on lung colony formation are due to a mitotic delay.
hyperoxia inhibits lung colony forming capacity in MT-7 but not in M109 cells.
the effects of hyperoxia were: 1) on the initial distribution of tumor cells in the lung; 2) on the number of lung tumor colonies formed; 3) on the cell cycle time of tumor cells in lung colonies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of hyperoxia and hypoxia on the growth characteristics of tumors in the lung and on the growth of tumors in the brain.
the effect of oxygen on the growth of tumor colonies in the lung, with the aim of understanding the mechanism(s) of oxygen toxicity in this organ.
the study of the effect of hyperoxia in lung metastasis formation by two tumor cell lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oxygen sensitivity of tumor cells depends on the tumor cell line and on the experimental conditions.
oxygen sensitivity of the tumor cell line is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the inhibition of lung colony formation in vivo by hyperoxia.
hyperoxia inhibits growth of MT-7 tumor cells by delaying the onset of DNA synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hyperoxia reduces the number of lung metastases by decreasing the growth fraction in the colonies that do develop.
hyperoxia does not modify the initial distribution of cells in the different phases of the cycle, but it does inhibit the transition from G2 to mitosis.
the oxygen sensitivity of tumor cells is a function of the cell cycle phase in which the oxygen-sensitive process is occurring.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the oxygen sensitivity of the cell cycle in vivo is a function of the oxygen sensitivity of a particular tumor cell line and that the oxygen sensitivity in vitro of a cell line does not necessarily predict its oxygen sensitivity in vivo.
the effects of oxygen on the growth of tumor cells in vivo may be different than the effects of oxygen observed in vitro.
the effects of oxygen on tumor growth in vivo are not the same as those in vitro.
